reference: Independently authored raw56 destination model and per-bit logical truth tables; no manufacturer or application programs
scope: All eight L: load destination views in ordinary RAM and sparse initialized windows, one shared EA/AGU update, full-state numerical flags and exact progress, REP, dirty parallel ALU operands, host aliases and visible real first faults
architectural_expectations: A10/B10 keep the old extension byte; full A/B sign-extend the 48-bit memory value; loads do not scale or limit
AB/BA sign-extend each 24-bit input into its accumulator, with zero low word; X/Y replace their full 48-bit bank
Both source guards/reads complete before any destination publishes; unknown Y cannot fabricate a successful transfer
Bounded rejected memory guards preserve owner state with no callbacks or AGU update
Unbounded failed transfers preserve the already advanced fetch PC and one actual AGU update; fault.pc retains the originating instruction
Parallel ALU inputs are pre-MOVE; logical ALU replaces only its middle word, preserving post-MOVE destination bits
Partial accumulator loads invalidate prior narrow-width proofs before following arithmetic saturation
negative_control: Same final test/fixture objects linked with the published previous archive; architectural checks pass before its first actual native-transfer assertion fails
fixture_corrections: Arithmetic-only sequence_model does not define XOR; use independent bfu truth tables with post-MOVE non-middle preservation. Atomic Core fetch advances PC before a later I/O fault (step_decoded/jit_moves and existing long-store first-fault fixtures); retain fault.pc at the originating address. No production CPU/fault semantics changed for either correction.

workloads.scope: Functional state and execution-path counters only; no qualified wall-time comparison
